mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profit visibility, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with PAYEMS growth exceeding 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, it indicates a tight labor market that accelerates consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates successful monetary easing without inflationary pressure, compressing equity discount rates and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (FEDFUNDS change * CPIAUCSL change) has a negative Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day returns are negative in >60% of instances where both series decline.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals deteriorating consumer confidence and economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and HOUST declines > 0.5% MoM, SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects robust manufacturing activity and supply chain efficiency, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with INDPRO growth exceeding 0.3% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1300.0 thousand units, it signals strong consumer confidence and economic momentum, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with HOUST > 1300.0.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflation that triggers anticipated monetary tightening, increasing equity discount rates and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with CPIAUCSL growth exceeding 0.2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.5%, it indicates economic weakness and reduced consumer spending power, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with UNRATE > 4.5%.
